text: Medieval written sources mention the existence of a church in the Mosfell Valley shortly after the adoption of Christianity. These sources, Egils Saga and The Saga of Gunnlaug Worms-Tongue, are from the 13th century. According to Egils Saga, Grim Svertingsson built a church at Mosfell after Christianity was adopted in Iceland. The Saga of Gunnlaug Worms-Tongue mentions that there was a church at Mosfell around A.D. 1010 and that it stood close to the farm house. If these sources are believed, the Mosfell church would be one of the earliest recorded churches in Iceland. For a long time people have wondered where the farm and the church of Mosfell had originally been situated. Some scholars have hypothesized that the farm of Mosfell was located originally where the farm of Hrísbrú is now. According to this theory, the farm and the church were moved later to the location where Mosfell is now, after which Hrísbrú developed as an independent farm.
